definition: to speak or write about something with great enthusiasm and praise

collocations.example: Critics rave about her latest novel and its bold style.
The new restaurant earned rave reviews from local food critics.

definition: a sharp instrument used for shaving hair from the skin

collocations.example: He changed the razor blade before shaving his thick beard.
She bought an electric razor for her father's birthday.

definition: to receive something, especially a benefit, as a result of your actions

collocations.example: Investors will eventually reap the benefits of their patience.
Hard workers eventually reap the rewards of their effort.

definition: to increase or recover in value or strength after a fall

collocations.example: Share prices rebounded sharply after the morning sell-off.
The economy began to rebound from its recent losses.

definition: to move back or gradually become more distant

collocations.example: The floodwaters began to recede once the storm passed.
The mountains seemed to recede into the distant haze.

definition: willing to listen to or accept new ideas or suggestions

collocations.example: She was always receptive to new ideas from her team.
He gave an impressive speech to a receptive audience.

definition: a part of a cell that receives and responds to chemical signals

collocations.example: Certain hormones bind to a specific hormone receptor in cells.
The drug blocks the receptor site on the cell surface.

definition: a period when work or an activity stops for a break

collocations.example: The students chatted happily in the yard at recess.
Congress is in recess until early next month.

definition: given or done in return, and shared equally by two sides

collocations.example: The two colleges have a reciprocal arrangement for exchange students.
They built a reciprocal relationship based on mutual trust.

definition: to exchange a coupon, voucher, or points for goods, money, or a discount

collocations.example: You can redeem this voucher at any of our stores.
She redeemed her points for a free flight ticket.

definition: the act of saving someone from error or making up for a fault

collocations.example: He felt his past mistakes were beyond redemption.
The disgraced athlete worked hard to seek redemption.

definition: a tall plant with slender stems that grows near water

collocations.example: Birds nest among the reeds along the river bank.
The lake was fringed with a thick reed bed.

definition: an automatic physical reaction to something, not controlled by thought

collocations.example: Blinking is a reflex action that protects the eyes.
The goalkeeper's quick reflexes saved the match.

definition: to stop yourself from doing something

collocations.example: Passengers must refrain from smoking inside the terminal building.
The official chose to refrain from comment on the case.

definition: a sum of money returned to you, especially for faulty or unwanted goods

collocations.example: The store offered me a full refund for the jacket.
You can request a refund within thirty days of purchase.

definition: to renovate and redecorate something, especially a building

collocations.example: The company plans to refurbish its aging office building.
They bought a fully refurbished apartment near the station.

definition: to grow or develop again after being damaged or lost

collocations.example: Some lizards can regenerate a tail after losing it.
Damaged liver cells can regenerate within a few weeks.

definition: an official list, or the office where official records are kept

collocations.example: The property was recorded at the local land registry.
They got married at the town registry office.

definition: to pay back money to someone that they have spent or lost

collocations.example: The company will reimburse all reasonable travel expenses.
We will reimburse you for any costs you incur.

definition: to return someone to a job or position they held before

collocations.example: The court ordered the firm to reinstate the dismissed worker.
He was reinstated in his old position after the appeal.

definition: to say something again in order to emphasize it

collocations.example: Let me reiterate that safety is our top priority.
The minister reiterated his support for the new policy.

definition: to move someone or something to a lower or less important position

collocations.example: The report was relegated to the bottom of the pile.
The team was relegated to a lower division this season.

definition: an object or custom that has survived from the past

collocations.example: The old mill is a relic of the town's industrial past.
Archaeologists discovered an ancient relic beneath the temple.

definition: to give up something such as power, control, or a possession

collocations.example: He refused to relinquish control of the family business.
She agreed to relinquish her claim to the property.

definition: a small remaining part or quantity of something

collocations.example: This custom is a remnant of a much older tradition.
They are the last remnant of an ancient people.

definition: to formally give up a claim, right, belief, or possession

collocations.example: The group agreed to renounce violence and join peace talks.
She chose to renounce her claim to the throne.

definition: to officially cancel a law so it no longer applies

collocations.example: The government decided to repeal the smoking ban.
Congress moved to repeal the entire act last year.

definition: to drive or keep something away

collocations.example: This spray is designed to repel insects and mosquitoes.
The troops managed to repel the enemy attack.

definition: the range of skills, works, or activities a person or group can perform

collocations.example: The pianist has a wide repertoire of classical pieces.
She added several new dishes to her repertoire.

definition: the ability to recover quickly from difficulties or setbacks

collocations.example: Regular challenges can help children build emotional resilience.
The community showed great resilience after the flood.

definition: a quality that makes something seem important or meaningful to people

collocations.example: The film's themes have a strong emotional resonance for viewers.
Her speech carried deep cultural resonance for the audience.

definition: a machine that helps a very ill person to breathe

collocations.example: The patient was placed on a respirator after surgery.
A mechanical respirator kept him breathing through the night.

definition: to slow down the progress or development of something

collocations.example: Cold weather can retard the growth of young plants.
Constant delays retarded the progress of the project.

definition: a quick, sharp, or angry reply

collocations.example: His sharp retort silenced everyone in the room.
She had a witty retort ready for every question.

definition: to enjoy something greatly and take great pleasure in it

collocations.example: The champions reveled in their hard-won success.
She seemed to revel in all the attention.

definition: a title of respect used before the name of a member of the clergy

collocations.example: The Reverend John Smith led the Sunday morning service.
The reverend mother welcomed the new nuns warmly.

definition: to return to a previous state, condition, or habit

collocations.example: Under stress, people often revert to old habits.
The settings will revert to the default after restarting.

definition: to have the same ending sound as another word

collocations.example: In this poem, the word moon rhymes with June.
Poets often choose words that rhyme at line endings.

definition: a clever and difficult question or puzzle that is asked for fun

collocations.example: No one could solve the ancient riddle of the sphinx.
The teacher posed a tricky riddle to the class.

definition: a small bird with a red or orange breast

collocations.example: A robin redbreast sang cheerfully in the garden hedge.
We watched a nesting robin feed her hungry chicks.

definition: behaving in an unexpected, uncontrolled, or dishonest way

collocations.example: The sanctions target several so-called rogue states.
A rogue trader lost millions through unauthorized deals.

definition: a red powder or cream used as makeup to color the cheeks

collocations.example: She applied a little rouge to brighten her cheeks.
A touch of rouge gave her pale face some color.

definition: to stir someone into being awake, active, or excited

collocations.example: The alarm failed to rouse him from a deep sleep.
Her passionate speech roused the crowd to action.

definition: broken pieces of stone, brick, and concrete from destroyed buildings

Rescuers searched for survivors buried under the rubble.

definition: a team sport played with an oval ball that players carry and kick

collocations.example: They play rugby every Saturday during the winter season.
We watched an exciting rugby match at the stadium.

definition: rough, rocky, and uneven, especially of land

collocations.example: The jeep struggled across the rugged mountain terrain.
We hiked along the wild, rugged coastline for hours.

definition: to make a soft, dry sound like leaves or paper moving

collocations.example: The dry leaves rustled gently in the autumn breeze.
Her silk dress rustled softly as she walked past.

definition: to sink, bend, or hang down, especially under weight

collocations.example: The old shelf began to sag under the heavy books.
The tent roof sagged in the middle after the rain.

definition: a long, complicated series of events, or a long story about them

collocations.example: He told us the whole saga of his delayed flight.

definition: a herb with gray-green leaves used in cooking

collocations.example: She flavored the stuffing with fresh sage leaves.
Add a pinch of dried sage to the sauce.

definition: most noticeable or important

collocations.example: The report summarized the salient features of the plan.
She raised one salient point during the meeting.

definition: a public bar, especially in the western United States

collocations.example: The cowboys gathered in the dusty town saloon.
He pushed open the swinging saloon doors and stepped inside.

definition: to rescue property or goods from loss or damage

collocations.example: Divers tried to salvage cargo from the sunken ship.
A major salvage operation recovered the wreck's valuables.

definition: a smooth fabric that is glossy and shiny on one side

collocations.example: She tied her hair back with a peach satin ribbon.
The bride wore a flowing gown of white satin.

definition: humor used to criticize people's faults or foolishness, especially in politics

collocations.example: The show is a sharp political satire on modern life.
His new novel is a biting satire of corporate greed.

definition: to enjoy something slowly and completely

collocations.example: She paused to savor the moment of her victory.
He ate slowly, savoring every bite of the meal.

definition: the skin that covers the top of the head, where hair grows

collocations.example: Cold weather can leave your scalp dry and itchy.
Gently massage the scalp when applying the shampoo.

definition: very little in amount, and not enough

collocations.example: The manager paid scant attention to staff complaints.
There is scant evidence to support his theory.

definition: of a bright red color

collocations.example: She wore a striking scarlet dress to the party.
He blushed scarlet when everyone turned to look.

definition: relating to schizophrenia, a serious mental illness affecting thought and perception

collocations.example: The clinic specializes in treating schizophrenic patients.
The doctor described his schizophrenic symptoms in careful detail.

definition: a cutting tool with two blades joined in the middle

collocations.example: Could you pass me a pair of scissors, please?
She trimmed her cuticles with small nail scissors.

definition: a strong feeling that someone or something is worthless or beneath respect

collocations.example: Critics poured scorn on the poorly made film.
She looked at the cheap imitation with scorn.

definition: an angry or bad-tempered expression on the face

collocations.example: A dark scowl crossed his face at the news.
She greeted the excuse with a scowl of disapproval.

definition: a loud, high, unpleasant sound or cry

collocations.example: The car stopped with a loud screech of tires.
The frightened child let out a piercing screech.

definition: to write or draw something quickly and carelessly

collocations.example: She scribbled a quick note and left it on the table.
He scribbled down the address before he forgot it.

definition: to move text or images up, down, or across a computer screen

collocations.example: Scroll down to the bottom of the page to continue.
She scrolled through her messages on the morning train.

definition: the act of keeping something secret or hidden from others

collocations.example: All the staff were sworn to secrecy about the merger.
The talks were conducted in complete secrecy.

definition: to produce and release a liquid or substance from a cell or gland

collocations.example: These glands secrete a fluid that aids digestion.
The cells secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.

definition: to flow or pass slowly through small openings

collocations.example: Water began to seep through the cracks in the wall.
Cold air was seeping into the room under the door.

definition: the act of officially taking control or possession of something

collocations.example: The court ordered the seizure of his bank assets.
Police reported a large drug seizure at the port.

definition: relating to the physical senses, such as sight, hearing, and touch

collocations.example: The brain processes sensory information from the eyes.
The skin is one of the body's main sensory organs.

definition: relating to the enjoyment of physical pleasure

collocations.example: Good food was one of his great sensual pleasures.
Soaking in a warm bath is a simple sensual pleasure.

definition: calm, peaceful, and untroubled

collocations.example: She greeted the bad news with a serene smile.
The garden had a wonderfully serene atmosphere at dawn.

definition: an underground pipe or channel that carries away waste water and sewage

collocations.example: Workers repaired the broken sewer pipe beneath the road.
The city is upgrading its aging sewer system this year.

definition: to cut the wool off a sheep

collocations.example: Farmers shear their sheep in early summer each year.
It takes real skill to shear the fleece quickly.

definition: a strong wine, originally from Spain, often drunk before a meal

collocations.example: She poured each guest a small glass of sherry.
He prefers a dry sherry before his dinner.

definition: to shine with a soft, wavering light

collocations.example: The hot road seemed to shimmer in the afternoon heat.
The calm sea shimmered with the early morning light.

definition: a fault or weakness in someone or something

collocations.example: The main shortcoming of the plan is its high cost.
She worked hard to overcome her shortcomings at work.

definition: a tool with a broad blade and handle used for digging or moving material

collocations.example: He grabbed a snow shovel to clear the driveway.
She dug the flowerbed with a small garden shovel.

definition: clever at understanding situations and making good decisions

collocations.example: He is a shrewd businessman with very sharp instincts.
Buying that property early was a shrewd investment.

definition: a loud, high cry or sound, often of fear or excitement

collocations.example: She let out a piercing shriek when she saw the spider.
A shriek of laughter came from the next room.

definition: to cover or hide something completely

collocations.example: Thick darkness shrouded the valley by nightfall.
Thick mist shrouded the hills early in the morning.

definition: a hinged cover or panel that closes over a window

collocations.example: She closed the shutters to keep out the afternoon sun.
The cottage had pretty blue wooden shutters on every window.

definition: a business or activity done in addition to one's main job

collocations.example: Selling crafts online became a lucrative sideline for her.
He runs a small catering business as a sideline.

definition: to examine something carefully in order to find what is useful or true

collocations.example: Investigators sifted through hundreds of documents for clues.
The committee carefully sifted the available evidence.

definition: the dark outline or shape of something seen against a lighter background

collocations.example: The mountains stood out in silhouette against the evening sky.
A dark silhouette appeared in the lighted doorway.

definition: seeming evil or threatening, as if something bad will happen

collocations.example: A sinister figure lurked in the shadows of the alley.
Police suspected a more sinister motive behind the fire.

definition: a device that makes a loud warning sound

collocations.example: The air-raid siren wailed across the city at midnight.
A police siren grew louder as the car approached.

definition: to read something quickly to get the main ideas

collocations.example: She skimmed through the newspaper during a quick breakfast.
He quickly skimmed the report before the morning meeting.

definition: very thin, often in an unattractive way

collocations.example: He was a tall, skinny boy with messy hair.
She had long, skinny legs like a ballet dancer.

definition: to kill someone or something in a violent way

collocations.example: In the legend, the knight set out to slay a dragon.
The hero vowed to slay the enemy and save the village.

definition: smooth, shiny, and stylish in appearance

collocations.example: The new phone has a sleek, slim design.
Their renovated office looked sleek and modern throughout.

definition: a band of cloth that supports an injured arm

collocations.example: He walked in with his broken arm in a sling.
She had to wear a sling after the shoulder surgery.

definition: a soft, comfortable shoe worn indoors

collocations.example: He shuffled to the kitchen in his old slippers.
She gave her grandmother warm, soft bedroom slippers.

definition: smooth or wet so that it is difficult to hold or walk on

collocations.example: Be careful, because the wet floor is very slippery.
The sign warns that the bridge is slippery when wet.

definition: a long, narrow cut or opening

collocations.example: She peered through a narrow slit in the fence.
Light came through a slit in the heavy curtains.

definition: to spill or splash over the edge of a container

collocations.example: The hot coffee slopped over the rim of the cup.
Water slopped onto the floor as he carried the bucket.

definition: a small, slow creature like a snail but without a shell

collocations.example: A garden slug had eaten holes in the lettuce leaves.
Slugs and snails damaged the young plants overnight.
